name: Magneto
summary: The villain who keeps having a point. Magneto, a Holocaust survivor and master of magnetism, believes mutants must defend themselves by any means, which puts him against his old friend Charles Xavier.
origin: Magneto might be the most sympathetic villain Marvel ever made, though it took a couple of decades to get there. In The X-Men #1 in 1963 he was a fairly standard menace in a cape, a mutant who could bend magnetism to his will and wanted mutants to rule. From 1981 onward Chris Claremont rebuilt him as a Holocaust survivor, later given the birth name Max Eisenhardt, whose fear of another genocide drives everything he does. That turned him from a cartoon tyrant into the X-Men's mirror image. He can move metal and twist magnetic fields, leave his body through astral projection, and wears a helmet that keeps telepaths out of his head.

storyline.title: Master of magnetism
storyline.beat: In X-Men #1 Magneto attacks a missile base, and soon after he founds the Brotherhood of Evil Mutants to fight for mutant rule.

storyline.title: A new depth
storyline.beat: Chris Claremont reveals that Magneto survived Auschwitz as a boy, reframing him as a man determined never to let his people be destroyed.

storyline.title: Running the school
storyline.beat: With Xavier dying, Magneto takes over the school and leads the New Mutants for a time.

storyline.title: The adamantium rip
storyline.beat: In one of the X-Men's most shocking moments, Magneto tears the adamantium out of Wolverine's skeleton.

storyline.title: Genosha falls
storyline.beat: The island nation of Genosha, which Magneto ruled, is wiped out by giant Sentinels.

storyline.title: Building a nation
storyline.beat: Magneto and Xavier found the mutant nation of Krakoa together, finally pursuing the same dream.

gossip.text: Magneto was always written as a Holocaust survivor.
gossip.truth: That backstory was not in his 1960s stories. Chris Claremont built it from 1981 onward.

gossip.text: He ripped the adamantium out of Wolverine's skeleton in X-Men #25 (1993).
Erik Lehnsherr is an alias. Later comics gave his birth name as Max Eisenhardt.
For decades comics named him the father of Quicksilver and the Scarlet Witch, until a 2015 storyline retconned it away.
Ian McKellen and Michael Fassbender both played him on film.

quiz.q: Whose adamantium did Magneto rip out in 1993?
quiz.why: He tore it from Wolverine in X-Men #25.

quiz.q: Which group did Magneto found in the early X-Men comics?

theme.tagline: Bends steel, bends rules, never bends the knee.

timeline.title: Master of magnetism
timeline.note: The X-Men #1 introduces Magneto attacking a missile base, the first villain the team ever faces.

timeline.title: A survivor's past
timeline.note: Uncanny X-Men #150 reveals Magneto lived through Auschwitz, giving his fury a painful source.

timeline.title: Running the school
timeline.note: Uncanny X-Men #200 puts Magneto on trial, and Xavier asks him to run the school in his place.

timeline.title: Fatal Attractions
timeline.note: X-Men #25 has Magneto rip the adamantium out of Wolverine's body, a shocking moment for the era.

timeline.title: Ian McKellen in X-Men
timeline.note: Bryan Singer's film casts Ian McKellen as Erik, opposite Patrick Stewart's Xavier.

timeline.title: Genosha falls
timeline.note: New X-Men #115 opens with giant Sentinels wiping out Magneto's mutant island nation of Genosha.

timeline.title: Building Krakoa
timeline.note: House of X has Magneto help Xavier found a mutant nation on the living island of Krakoa.

timeline.title: Leading in X-Men '97
timeline.note: The X-Men '97 revival puts Magneto in charge of the team, carrying out Xavier's will.
